graph.summary: donepezil → Acetylcholinesterase → Acetylcholine → chemical synaptic transmission → Alzheimer's Disease

evidence.snippet: donepezil, a highly selective (IC(50) = 6.7 nM) centrally acting reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that has been approved by FDA for treating cognitive deficit states such as in Alzheimer's disease
evidence.explanation: Donepezil is a reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, decreasing the enzyme's activity.

paper.title: Assessing the prospect of donepezil in improving cognitive impairment in patients with schizophrenia.

evidence.snippet: Enzymatic hydrolysis of acetylcholine in the synaptic cleft is fast and quickly metabolizes to choline and acetate by acetylcholinesterase.
evidence.explanation: Acetylcholinesterase hydrolyzes acetylcholine; its inhibition by donepezil therefore raises acetylcholine levels.

paper.title: Quantification of acetylcholine, an essential neurotransmitter, in brain microdialysis samples by liquid chromatography mass spectrometry.

evidence.snippet: Acetylcholine (ACh), an ubiquitous mediator substance broadly expressed in nature, acts as neurotransmitter in cholinergic synapses, generating specific communications
evidence.explanation: Acetylcholine acts as a neurotransmitter at cholinergic synapses, mediating synaptic transmission.

paper.title: Ultrafast and Slow Cholinergic Transmission. Different Involvement of Acetylcholinesterase Molecular Forms.

evidence.snippet: Cholinesterase inhibitors, such as donepezil and rivastigmine, increase acetylcholine (ACh) levels to enhance cognitive function in individuals with mild to moderate AD.
evidence.explanation: Restoring cholinergic synaptic transmission via increased acetylcholine enhances cognitive function in Alzheimer's disease.

paper.title: Exploring Alzheimer's disease treatment: Established therapies and novel strategies for future care.
